scope: Runtime, CI and development-resource optimization register. Source references describe implementation; evidence describes qualification.

entries.title: Unload hidden presentation
entries.invariant: Suspend after 60 continuous hidden seconds; preserve active work and restore query/selection identity.
entries.next_step: Measure engine/native footprint before hiding, after the deadline, and after repeated reopen; widget/cache disposal is not qualification.

entries.title: History cache invalidation and stale response protection
entries.invariant: Suspension releases retained payloads; late responses cannot refill released state.
entries.next_step: Add cancellation and byte-accounted admission without weakening stale-response guards.

entries.title: Lazy Quick Paste engine with retirement
entries.invariant: Create on demand, dispose Dart owners and native engine on retirement; preserve focus and paste behavior. Standard keyboard and native window close use the existing cancellation/hide/retirement paths. macOS Command-W and Option-Command-W invalidate the popup paste session before acknowledged retirement. Windows preserves the native system-menu close command. Linux GTK close/iconify coalesces duplicate requests, cancels/restores the transaction, and exits on idle; its callback is owned and released by the GTK window. Quit from the Linux popup requests primary-process termination through PID/transaction authorization. No event monitor, polling timer, retained presentation, or engine prewarming is introduced.
entries.next_step: Measure startup latency, peak and recovered memory for 100 open/close cycles; compare reuse only with evidence.

entries.title: Inference process isolation and idle teardown
entries.invariant: Model loading is lazy; idle worker exits after 60 seconds; disable/change/shutdown cancel and reap.
entries.next_step: Measure parent plus worker, model cold start, reuse, cancellation and recovery on each platform.

entries.title: OCR teardown after every invocation
entries.invariant: OCR success/error releases its worker; subsequent requests reload; semantic reuse stays separate.
entries.next_step: Collect controlled macOS comparison after the other test task ends; Android/Windows native evidence and unresolved budgets remain open.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One OCR invocation; ten routes execute unchanged. Prepared RGB crops are released after recognition, and tensor scores are borrowed rather than cloned.
entries.tradeoffs: Oversized crops are reconstructed instead of retained. All 840 compared per-route texts and confidence bit patterns matched. Preliminary timing/resource samples had concurrent external test load and are not controlled performance evidence.

entries.title: Bounded semantic cache and queue
entries.invariant: 32-entry query/cache bounds, latest query priority, lexical results while inference is pending.
entries.next_step: Measure sustained indexing and repeated queries; separately bound AI peak and return to ordinary budget.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Scores are Arc-shared only for an exact model scope, query vector/threshold bits, database generation and semantic revision. Clear on semantic service disable/stop/scope change and restore.
entries.tradeoffs: Accounting controls retained cache data, not total allocator/native memory. Semantic vector/document mutations add transactional revision updates; pin-only and file-chunk writes do not invalidate scores.

entries.title: Signed model downloads are streamed
entries.invariant: Download with a 64 KiB transfer buffer, declared-size/hash checks, cancellation and staged publication.
entries.next_step: Measure install/update network, disk and cancellation cleanup; include staging disk usage.

entries.title: Bounded IPC clients, frames and watches
entries.invariant: 64 clients, 8 watchers, 32 MiB frame cap and read/write deadlines.
entries.next_step: Add aggregate byte/concurrency admission: per-connection limits do not imply a 300 MB application ceiling.

entries.title: History page count and payload bounds
entries.invariant: Per-page count and aggregate content bounds; lazy previews.
entries.next_step: Keep these limits while adding a client-side page window; verify large-history navigation and selection.

entries.title: Image decode limits and scaled previews
entries.invariant: Bound individual decode allocations and thumbnail dimensions; avoid full-image list payloads.
entries.next_step: Budget concurrent decoded surfaces, encoded bytes, IPC/base64 copies, Flutter images and GPU/native surfaces together.

entries.title: Bounded source application icon metadata
entries.invariant: 32 KiB PNG, 128 px decoded edge, bounded metadata envelopes.
entries.next_step: Retain identity parity and bound resident icon caches by bytes and visible working set.

entries.title: SQLite connection/page-cache and retention controls
entries.invariant: One minimum idle connection, up to four pooled connections, an 8 MiB configured page-cache target per connection, and batched retention; cache targets are not hard total-memory bounds.
entries.next_step: Measure sustained full-app storage and sync workloads, connection retirement, encrypted temporary state and platform-native memory. Preserve four-way checkout and existing timeouts.
entries.allocation_lifetime: The file-backed pool initially maintains one idle connection and can grow lazily to the unchanged maximum of four. Existing 600-second idle timeout and connection lifetime remain unchanged; in-memory pools retain their no-retirement policy.

bounds.total_memory: Page-cache settings are targets, not hard process-memory bounds.

entries.cancellation: Existing pool checkout, connection retirement and application shutdown behavior is preserved.
entries.tradeoffs: Initial concurrent work can open more connections lazily. Native combined-candidate startup/read data is recorded; it does not isolate pool savings. First binary launch cache state differs and cannot establish a startup regression or improvement.

entries.title: Adaptive peer synchronization cadence
entries.invariant: One daemon/Android scheduler: 60-second no-peer wait, shared 5–10-second adaptive cadence, capture wake queued behind manual rounds, live disable cancellation, and joined session teardown. Preserve convergence.
entries.next_step: Measure idle with no peers, reachable peers, offline peers and reconnect; preserve sync latency.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One outgoing round; per-peer tasks exist only while its sessions run. Cancelled sessions are aborted and joined before releasing the round permit.
entries.cancellation: Sync disable cancels the live SyncCycle; shutdown and new capture wakes abort and join unfinished sessions. Capture wake is preserved for the next round.

bounds.peer_tasks: One per dialable paired peer, retaining existing fanout; active network sessions use the shared Node admission limit.
bounds.idle_timing: Existing AdaptiveCadence constants and NO_PEERS_INTERVAL; allocation policy, not a measured runtime budget.

entries.tradeoffs: Android now shares the desktop no-peer wait and adaptive idle policy. Native latency, wakeup, CPU and memory effects remain unmeasured.

entries.title: Bounded sync protocol messages
entries.invariant: Summary pages/items/messages have individual bounds.
entries.next_step: RUN-054 supplies the bounded encrypted session workspace and complete catch-up tests; measure native supported-platform scaling and transfer latency.
entries.functional_validation: Protocol bounds retained; 316 P2P tests and real 5000-row StoreSource catch-up tests passed with RUN-054.

session_workspace_attempt.reason: Real 5000-row catch-up stopped at 2000 rows after six rounds. Baseline cause was not established; no resource saving is claimed.

entries.title: Bounded runtime event broadcasts
entries.invariant: Finite event rings with lag recovery, not an unbounded queue.
entries.next_step: Stress slow consumers and preserve refresh/recovery correctness.

entries.title: Android sequential ingestion and bitmap limits
entries.invariant: One ingestion worker, 32 queue entries, 16 MiB encoded and 50 MiB decoded image caps.
entries.next_step: Collect controlled macOS comparison after the other test task ends; Android/Windows native evidence and unresolved budgets remain open.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Owned encoded PNG backing buffer crosses JNI with an explicit valid length; Rust copies only that prefix. Shared image admission covers source read, normalization and JNI ingestion.

entries.title: Android capture and SMS lifecycle cleanup
entries.invariant: Stop observers/threads on lifecycle end; SMS provider query capped at 32 rows and bounded bodies.
entries.next_step: Validate physical-device idle, bursts, permissions, service restart and return to baseline.

entries.title: Bounded origin metadata reads
entries.invariant: Resolve page origins with bounded bulk metadata reads instead of per-item N+1 lookups.
entries.next_step: Measure history query latency and DB work as history size grows.

entries.title: Bound visible history pages and total media bytes
entries.invariant: Bound retained pages, preview/icon/spoiler bytes and in-flight work without truncating navigable history.
entries.next_step: Native process-family observations are developer diagnostics; missing supported-platform evidence and unresolved budgets prevent resource qualification.
entries.last_wave_disposition: The earlier rejected centered/eager-page prototypes were replaced with lazy SliverList/ListView windows, saved-cursor refetch, independent Quick Paste lanes, surviving visible anchors and preserved evicted pin metadata.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Resident summaries are page-window owned; suspend/query reset releases summaries and media. Visited cursor/ID/pin/date metadata remains compact while navigating; visible selection owns its detail separately.
entries.tradeoffs: Incoming and protected visible regions, or a single oversized visible page, can exceed targets temporarily. Compact visited metadata still grows with visited history. Unseen rows use ordinary lazy-scroll extent estimates; measured visible anchors are restored after eviction/refetch. These controls are not a hard native-memory ceiling.
entries.combined_diagnostic_attribution: One incremental e9-to-34ab combined-candidate pair, not per-optimization attribution. Same 10000-item fixture, 1500 ordered logical IDs, first-row selection and viewport, four images and lifecycle phases. Resident summaries 1500 to 150; see raw process-family/role counters. OS cache/background uncontrolled; no stable speedup or resource qualification claim.

entries.title: Shared memory admission for image and IPC work
entries.invariant: Per-operation limits and parallelism must fit a common process-tree envelope.
entries.next_step: Keep measuring representative UI scrolling, inspector and full process-family scenarios. Aggregate bytes, visible-request priority, complete cancellation and supported-platform native evidence remain open.

measured_saving.scenario: 32 preview requests per group, 2048x2048 4-bit PNG; 32 mixed history/status reads at concurrency 4
measured_saving.attribution: Combined daemon candidate including lazy SQLite connections; not an isolated per-change saving or total-app measurement.

entries.allocation_lifetime: Charge frame growth before allocation; drop raw request text after parsing while transferring credit through queued requests, running blocking jobs and response writes. Copy/control lanes are reserved from bulk pressure. Image preview scope releases both encrypted source row and decrypted source bytes before PNG base64 response encoding.
entries.cancellation: Dropping queued admission releases its waiter. A started blocking closure owns its permit until actual completion, including caller cancellation and errors. Other request classes, capture, paste and sync do not acquire this semaphore.
entries.tradeoffs: Wire credits and weighted handler classes do not establish a hard bound for all decoded, legacy first-row, module/network or native allocations. Large Add input can be refused under saturated inbound bulk. Quick Paste preload and display share DPR-bounded preview/decode keys; renderer/native memory still requires process-family measurement.

entries.title: Suspend UI polling and prevent overlapping refresh
entries.invariant: No presentation-only periodic work while hidden; no overlapping capture refresh.
entries.next_step: Collect controlled macOS comparison after the other test task ends; Android/Windows native evidence and unresolved budgets remain open.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Retained destinations preserve state; fully hidden tabs disable tickers. Settings-only work runs only for the visible selected Settings destination; tray/capture authority remains independent.
entries.tradeoffs: Partly visible swipe destinations retain ticking. State and current values are preserved on return.

entries.title: Page Android screenshot backlog
entries.invariant: Bound metadata candidates per scan without dropping eligible screenshots or replaying private-mode content.
entries.next_step: Screenshot candidates are processed in pages of 32 with timestamp/ID continuation; failed/pending rows are reconsidered in later scans.

entries.title: Bound Android cleanup executors
entries.invariant: Bound cleanup/drain threads and backlog while maintaining prompt cancellation and stream closure.
entries.next_step: Collect controlled macOS comparison after the other test task ends; Android/Windows native evidence and unresolved budgets remain open.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Host/input reservations include their eventual cleanup. Text/pending leases remain held until snapshotting or running work actually exits; queued cancellation releases exactly once.
entries.tradeoffs: New captures may be refused at existing overload boundaries. Explicit capture reports failure. No accepted drain/close job is dropped and no blocking cleanup runs on the UI thread.

entries.title: Memory-pressure and native-retention investigation
entries.invariant: Releasing Dart references is distinct from reclaiming allocator, engine, GPU or native memory.
entries.next_step: Use equivalent native observations for retention attribution; missing budgets/platform/scenario evidence prevent qualification.
entries.last_wave_decision: Primary engine lifetime and executor counts remain unchanged. Main engines own OS channels/window/tray/shortcut integration. Existing UI stack captures showed under 1.2 MiB resident against 57.5 MiB reserved virtual stack space; this does not attribute daemon executor cost or justify shrinking pools.
entries.tradeoffs: A18 retains in-progress pairing/dialog/camera/user-operation state. Native allocator/GPU recovery is distinct from Dart object release.

entries.title: Runtime budgets, scenario receipts and release gate
entries.invariant: Ordinary application-wide memory <300 MB; separate AI peak/recovery; fail closed on missing platform evidence.
entries.next_step: Read-only macOS process-family diagnostics and offline validation exist. Establish missing budgets, scenario durations, trusted release provenance, Android/Windows collectors, network/GPU attribution and publication wiring before release qualification.

entries.title: One optimization register and evidence lifecycle
entries.invariant: Every optimization has a stable ID, owner, contract, tests, tradeoffs and exact evidence; implementation is not measured qualification.
entries.next_step: This register owns optimization status. Runtime and CI contracts own their respective thresholds.

entries.title: CI architecture and cache isolation
entries.invariant: Preserve release artifact/signing identity; cache trust separation and platform matrix.
entries.next_step: Keep existing gates; attach equivalent-input cold/warm/unknown-cohort evidence before any acceleration claim.

entries.title: CI timing telemetry and investigation budgets
entries.invariant: Wall-clock, critical path and cache evidence stay separate from runtime RAM.
entries.next_step: Continue recording CI changes with scripts/ci/metrics.py; it currently has no native runtime memory ingestion.

entries.next_step: Track reclaimed disk versus subsequent cold build CPU/time; the documented policy is not a continuous disk ceiling.

entries.next_step: Verify hook implementation against both ADRs before assigning active/superseded status; avoid counting old policy as a current optimization.

entries.invariant: Each main and Quick Paste engine applies a 16 MiB decoded image cache, 128 entries, and a 16 MiB Skia cache request. macOS selects Skia Metal; backend acknowledgement alone is not proof of enforcement.
entries.next_step: The macOS v3 diagnostic still exceeded the combined budget at 333.3 MB; measure live surfaces and every supported backend. No aggregate bound is claimed.

entries.next_step: Bound reloadable History page ownership without dropping access, selection, or reorder behavior. Measure large text and sustained pagination.
entries.native_diagnostic_status: macOS candidate 5: ordinary peak 321144968 bytes; budget failed; Android/Windows unavailable

entries.next_step: Measure equivalent filter/inspector/resize cycles, CPU and GPU retention. Bound in-flight payload admission independently of cache ownership.

entries.next_step: Repeat native hide/show with accessibility and Quick Paste on every platform. The overall macOS ordinary workload still exceeds the 300 MB budget.
entries.functional_validation: 16 lifecycle/root tests passed; macOS candidate 5 survived hidden AX read and restored Image filter and fixture selection

entries.title: Release macOS allocator-retained image decode scratch pages
entries.owner_module: Core image preview and native allocation lifecycle
entries.invariant: Freed full-resolution and thumbnail RGBA scratch buffers must not keep the ordinary process family above its budget after preview work completes. Preserve image quality, errors and concurrent-request correctness.
entries.next_step: Startup policy natively confirmed: daemon recovery 51,020,808 -> 14,107,560 bytes for the same 4K PNG workload. Candidate 7 total UI restore still peaked at 318,703,656 bytes because live decode overlapped UI surfaces; RUN-030 addresses that separately. Complete platform/scenario qualification remains required.

measured_saving.scenario: four warmups + twenty 4K PNG previews + five-second recovery

entries.functional_validation: Two allocator-startup unit tests passed; native --version and inference-worker EOF passed; Candidate 7 daemon exited when its UI parent was terminated. Twenty preview hashes unchanged. Median latency 24.47 -> 25.76 ms.

entries.title: Stream ordinary PNG thumbnail pixels through a bounded row window
entries.invariant: Use the existing image-rs thumbnail sampler and PNG encoder with a <=1MiB row window; preserve decoded-size acceptance, aspect ratio, no-upscale and byte-identical previews. Interlaced, animated,16-bit and oversized-window shapes retain the existing bounded decoder.
entries.next_step: Native isolated preview workload confirms lower daemon peak and byte-identical output. Complete History/hide/restore UI validation, fallback-format coverage, and native Android/Windows measurements. Profile observed CPU/latency increase before further tuning.

measured_saving.metric: sampled daemon active physical footprint bytes

Twenty native preview response hashes match baseline. Median latency increased 25.76 -> 35.95 ms; sampled daemon CPU for workload/recovery increased 0.622 -> 0.866 seconds. Candidate 8: 24 native inspector opens verified, 180s sampled family peak 286,918,648 bytes. Functional restore passed but restore peak was outside collection; hidden suspension not established.

entries.title: Reuse the transient Quick Paste engine for tray history
entries.invariant: Tray and shortcut share the existing lazy Quick Paste engine, repository, bounded media caches, paging, and paste session. Tray height is capped at 600 logical pixels and available work area; only the list scrolls. No independent history snapshot, watch lease, polling loop, or persistent engine is introduced. The existing acknowledged shutdown releases the repository and native engine after dismissal or paste.
entries.next_step: Verify tray placement, every clip kind, and focus-safe paste on installed macOS and Windows. Measure application, daemon, and workers separately and together for tray/shortcut cycles, peak, steady state, recovery, and growth. Non-memory budgets and native qualification remain unresolved.
entries.functional_validation: 160 targeted Flutter tests passed, including all 13 clip kinds at 600 logical pixels; Dart analysis passed. Native Swift geometry scenarios and portable Windows geometry scenarios passed, including a short secondary monitor, top/bottom trays, inspector height, and 200-percent dimensions. macOS Dev debug build passed. Installed-platform interaction and native resource qualification remain pending.

entries.title: Remove redundant Quick Paste startup work and unchanged spoiler notifications
entries.owner_module: Quick Paste startup and shared spoiler state
entries.invariant: Quick Paste reuses its initial watched page for its first presentation and omits unused facets. Preference reads overlap safely, and module metadata starts only when the inspector needs it; pending metadata never blocks showing or closing the inspector. An unchanged spoiler update neither advances the revision nor wakes clients, while actual changes retain the existing shared-state notifications. Engine creation remains on demand with the existing acknowledged retirement; no persistent engine or new cache is introduced. Completed inspector metadata is refreshed on each inspector opening; simultaneous openings share one pending read. OCR revalidates module metadata before preparing image bytes or invoking a worker. No timer or idle metadata polling is introduced.
entries.next_step: Compare baseline and candidate native click-to-window, first-frame, and preview latency with equivalent debug/AOT builds and cache state. Measure process-family memory, CPU, wakeups, and I/O on macOS, physical Android, and installed Windows. Native interaction measurement was not authorized in this task; non-memory budgets remain unresolved.
entries.functional_validation: 168 targeted Flutter tests, 6 Rust tests, Dart analysis, and macOS Dev debug build passed. A deterministic first-open regression observed two History queries before the change and one after it, with zero unused facet queries. Slow inspector metadata never blocks presentation. Actual spoiler changes still notify both clients. Native click-to-frame latency and resource savings remain unmeasured. Status freshness follow-up: 1162 Flutter unit/widget tests and static analysis passed in the isolated mocked harness; native behavior and resource qualification remain unestablished.
entries.tradeoffs: Freshness adds one module-metadata read per inspector opening and one before explicit OCR recognition. Reads replace the existing snapshot and do not retain additional module lists or start inference. Pending metadata never blocks popup presentation. Native memory, CPU, I/O and latency effects remain unmeasured; no resource saving or qualification is claimed.

entries.title: Present Quick Paste only after its visible media frame is ready
entries.invariant: Position the on-demand popup while hidden, decode only mounted viewport media through existing bounded caches, submit its frame, then reveal by the current presentation ID. A changed foreground or superseded ID cannot activate an obsolete popup. Offscreen clips and image errors do not hold the reveal. macOS registers only file-selection and preferences plugins; Windows registers only file-selection. Existing shutdown retires the engine and owned repository, with no prewarming or persistent engine. Flutter decoded-cache limits remain unchanged.
entries.next_step: Measure native click-to-ready and first-visible-frame latency, including decode, with equivalent debug/AOT builds, fixture, and cache state. Compare peak/steady/recovery process-family memory, CPU, wakeups and I/O for cold openings and repeated cycles on macOS and installed Windows. Computer Use remains unauthorized; native latency/resource qualification is not established and non-memory budgets remain unresolved.
entries.functional_validation: 172 targeted Flutter tests, Dart analysis, and macOS Dev debug build passed. Visible image decoding gates the native reveal; offscreen images do not delay it; superseded IDs cannot reveal. Windows hidden preparation regression added but not run on Windows. Native UI interaction and latency/resource qualification remain pending.

entries.title: Route macOS tray activation directly through the native Quick Paste opener
entries.invariant: Bind the existing status button primary action directly to the shared native opener after leaving AppKit tracking. Capture the application target and icon frame at the click. Preserve the original target for context-menu gestures and restore only the owned target on detach. Detach cancels queued activation before releasing the tray. The binding retains no button or application payload, adds no poller/event monitor/engine, and preserves acknowledged Quick Paste retirement.
entries.next_step: Compare tray and shortcut in the same bundle/build with equivalent workload and cache state. A temporary separate Dev shortcut and source-tagged diagnostic traces confirmed that the observed delay also occurs through the Dev shortcut; the shortcut was restored and diagnostic code removed after comparison. Complete native latency/resource qualification remains unestablished and non-memory budgets unresolved.
entries.functional_validation: Final integrated validation passed: full Flutter analysis, formatting, 267 targeted Flutter tests including History/spoiler layouts, 6 Rust spoiler/event tests, windowless native Cocoa tray checks, and macOS Dev debug build. Temporary instrumentation and comparison shortcut were removed/restored before commit. Installed Windows and physical Android evidence and complete native resource qualification remain missing.

entries.title: Bound on-demand file materialization for Quick Paste
entries.invariant: File bytes are materialized only on an explicit action. Production Quick Paste reuses native-recorded, verified durable downloaded paths across engines and presentations; a missing path triggers a new transfer. Legacy repository adapters retain the bounded temporary preparation cache and polling fallback.
entries.next_step: Measure temporary disk use and transfer CPU, I/O, peak memory, and cleanup across supported platforms. Confirm behavior on installed macOS, Windows, and Android builds; native resource qualification is not established.
entries.functional_validation: Targeted Flutter and Rust tests cover transfer progress, cancellation, reuse, and remote clipboard fallback; installed-platform and native resource evidence remain pending.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Production downloads are user-kept destinations with recorded links, not expiring staging copies. Legacy preparation retains one fresh cached reference and scoped staging leases; byte buffers remain bounded.
entries.tradeoffs: RUN-056 supersedes production temporary-copy expiry with persistent user-visible downloads. Native process-family and disk/resource qualification remain pending.

entries.title: Owned temporary payload cleanup and encrypted database reclamation
entries.invariant: Preserve original History bytes, pins, retention settings and live clear boundaries. Current Android URI ownership survives restart and interrupted publication; stale inactive publications have one-day grace. Flutter staging is namespaced, leased across processes and protected across engines. No periodic cleanup timer or permanent cleanup executor. Recognized installed-version packages are removed offline; newer pending installers remain. Completed transfer paths identify actual bytes; only complete outputs are published. New databases reclaim incrementally after committed deletes; legacy full rebuild requires exclusive lifetime Store ownership before runtime publication. Android, macOS and Windows storage/module cleanup use the shared advisory-lock adapter; Android uses flock because Rust std file locking is unsupported there. Module managers retain shared lifetime leases; exclusive startup maintenance removes only expired default temporary input/extraction/download directories, preserving installed models and completed pending module updates.
entries.next_step: Measure equivalent native baseline/candidate cache and data growth, CPU, I/O, startup/action latency, process-family memory and low-space behavior on macOS, physical Android and installed Windows. A legacy file opened before a large deletion requires a later exclusive reopen; conversion admission requires 8 MiB and 25% free pages. Busy readers can defer WAL truncation. Unmarked generic legacy desktop staging is preserved because ownership is unknown. Recent/current/leased payloads and pending newer installers have no aggregate byte ceiling. Allocation policies are not resource budgets; unresolved non-memory thresholds remain unresolved.
entries.functional_validation: 454 core Rust tests, 45 module tests and 224 targeted Flutter tests passed in dirty workspace snapshots; Flutter analysis and owned-source formatting passed. Two existing asset-dependent native module tests remain ignored by their pre-existing definitions. Android host tests could not run: the Android native build is blocked by parallel JNI/generated-binding changes (including missing JString import). User explicitly instructed this task to leave parallel code unchanged and record the blocker. No installed candidate or native resource qualification is established.

entries.title: Explicit bounded file transfer
entries.owner_module: Shared file offers, encrypted chunk store and authenticated peer sessions
entries.invariant: Ordinary P2P/cloud history sync transfers only an authenticated file offer. File bodies move only for an explicit Download. Import, encryption, save and native copy use bounded blocks; no file-sized allocation for new files. One explicit outgoing/incoming file session per node. Cancellation, revocation and shutdown close sessions; partial destinations and scoped plaintext are removed. Encrypted chunks share a digest and are released with the final retained row. File byte quota includes retained bodies. A downloaded destination is user-owned and has no second hidden full-byte cache.
entries.allocation_lifetime: 64 KiB plaintext blocks while actively importing, serving, downloading or copying. Existing small inline rows are converted before sync starts; legacy decryption remains bounded by the former 4 MiB cap.
entries.cancellation: Explicit Cancel, pairing removal/revocation and runtime shutdown cancel active downloads. Reads have the existing peer deadline.

bounds.file_limit: Live editable max_file_size_bytes; default 64 MiB, supported setting range 1 MiB through 20 GiB. This is an allocation policy, not a native resource budget.

entries.tradeoffs: Import hashes then encrypts the source and holds one SQLite write transaction for the snapshot. One authenticated size-checked request starts a bounded binary stream; storage chunks remain 64 KiB without a per-chunk network round trip. The source must be online for an uncached download. Native clipboard staging retains its existing timed cleanup owner.
entries.next_step: Collect equivalent baseline/candidate native peak, steady, recovery, growth, CPU, latency and I/O evidence on macOS, physical Android and installed Windows. Resolve unset runtime budgets before resource qualification.

entries.title: Shared bounded GitHub release-asset transport
entries.invariant: One trusted HTTPS authority and redirect policy for app and module artifacts. Stream through IOSink backpressure, hash received bytes in the same pass, enforce declared and streamed size bounds, remove failed partial files, and preserve signature validation before use. Repository-specific metadata, staging and cache publication remain with their owner.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Only the current HTTP stream and sink buffers during an active download; no whole-package byte list or retained payload.

bounds.artifact_limits: Existing app, module, metadata and signature size limits; unchanged.

entries.cancellation: Network timeout, stream or integrity failure closes the output and removes its partial destination. Repository disposal force-closes its HttpClient.
entries.tradeoffs: Disk and hash work share one streamed pass; physical buffer sizes remain owned by dart:io. Native memory, CPU, latency and I/O effects are unmeasured.
entries.next_step: Measure equivalent baseline/candidate downloads and failure cleanup on macOS, physical Android and installed Windows; resolve pending resource budgets before qualification.

entries.title: Reuse immutable History row snapshots
entries.invariant: Repeated reads reuse one immutable canonical row list until row mutation. Previously exposed snapshots remain immutable; selection, order, pagination and watch behavior remain unchanged.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Canonical rows live until refresh, mutation, suspend or controller disposal; in-place mutations copy only a frozen list. Wholesale replacement and clear do not clone the old list.

bounds.internally_retained_row_arrays: One canonical array; external widgets may retain earlier immutable snapshots.
bounds.history_page_window: Unchanged and still open work in RUN-019.

entries.cancellation: Existing query epochs, watch cancellation and suspension are preserved.
entries.tradeoffs: Unchanged refreshes preserve both canonical snapshot and individual row identities after comparing all exposed fields, avoiding downstream Quick Paste cache invalidation.
entries.next_step: Collect controlled macOS comparison after the other test task ends; Android/Windows native evidence and unresolved budgets remain open.

entries.title: Reuse presentation-owned syntax highlighting
entries.invariant: Identical source, JSON mode and theme reuse the exact highlighted result without changing detection, spans or visible text.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One memo result belongs to each mounted row or inspector, clears on owner disposal, clip identity/non-code changes, and source/theme replacement; no process-global source cache.

bounds.oversized_sources: Rendered using existing behavior and not memoized.

entries.cancellation: Presentation disposal clears memo ownership; there are no new workers or asynchronous jobs.
entries.tradeoffs: Retains the current TextSpan while its existing presentation owner is alive; avoids repeated detection/rendering. Framework/native text allocations need native attribution. Native inspector timing and UI-harness memory had substantial variation; no causal CPU/RAM saving is established for the memo in isolation.
entries.next_step: Android and Windows native measurements and unresolved non-memory budgets remain required before qualification.

entries.title: Bound repeated Quick Paste text and shortcut work
entries.invariant: Preserve visible order, platform shortcut assignment, persistence and Unicode/RTL ellipsis. Shortcut lookup uses a cached reverse map; unrelated History notifications do not enqueue redundant pin reconciliation.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Derived rows and maps belong to the popup controller/current data revision. Each ellipsis call owns one reusable TextPainter and disposes it in finally.

bounds.derived_data: One current items snapshot, shortcut map and reverse lookup per controller; existing navigable history limits are unchanged.

entries.cancellation: Existing serialized shortcut persistence and disposal checks remain; changes arriving during queued writes are reconciled.
entries.tradeoffs: Caches derived metadata while the popup controller exists. Requires shortcut race/failure, pin/delete and platform-key tests; does not change sync or OCR.
entries.next_step: Android and Windows native measurements and unresolved non-memory budgets remain required before qualification.

entries.title: Localize History file download progress notifications
entries.invariant: Byte progress uses dedicated feature signals consumed by the transfer manager, Quick Paste status and selected inspector controls. It does not rebuild History or requery durable history per percentage; terminal state changes remain general notifications.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One progress signal per controller and existing active-download progress values; values are removed after completion and signal is disposed with the controller.

bounds.progress_entries: Existing active downloads only; no per-clip notifier cache.

entries.cancellation: Disposed-controller callbacks are ignored; existing save cancellation and error propagation remain.
entries.tradeoffs: Typed writer events now drive only the dedicated progress signal; general start/fail/cancel/finish behavior remains unchanged. Legacy capability still uses the original polling fallback.
entries.next_step: Android and Windows native measurements and unresolved non-memory budgets remain required before qualification.

entries.title: Suppress unchanged Settings refresh notifications
entries.invariant: Suppress unchanged successful state notifications. Typed capable backends update capture state from revisioned events; legacy and disconnected cases retain three-second polling.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Only current capture/sync comparison snapshots are retained; mutable peer and health lists are copied so later in-place changes remain observable.

bounds.comparison_state: One current raw capture snapshot and one accepted sync snapshot, each bounded by existing live-state collections; no historical snapshots are accumulated.

entries.cancellation: Existing single-flight, presentation-epoch, busy and disposal guards remain.
entries.tradeoffs: Avoids full UI notifications for unchanged successful polls at the cost of small bounded comparison snapshots. Does not remove required polling or alter sync cadence. Native isolated saving is unmeasured.
entries.next_step: Measure the isolated runtime effect and full-app scenarios on supported platforms; unresolved budgets and missing native evidence prevent qualification.

entries.title: Use one filesystem probe per file progress tick
entries.invariant: Legacy progress fallback performs one stat per tick; typed runtime backends instead consume writer progress events.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One current FileStat result during the existing active-save progress callback.
entries.cancellation: Existing timer cancellation, partial-file rollback and caller cancellation are unchanged.
entries.tradeoffs: Source-level reduction from two filesystem probes to one per active tick. No isolated native CPU or IO saving is claimed; event-driven writer progress remains separate work.
entries.next_step: Measure the isolated runtime effect and full-app scenarios on supported platforms; unresolved budgets and missing native evidence prevent qualification.

entries.title: Transfer binary preview bytes into Flutter
entries.invariant: Identical image/icon bytes and dimensions; daemon IPC JSON remains compatible.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Rust decodes daemon base64 once; generated bridge delivers Uint8List to current presentation owners.
entries.cancellation: Owned resources remain alive through actual work completion and release on owner teardown.
entries.tradeoffs: Removes Dart base64 strings/decoding on this boundary; isolated native savings are unmeasured.
entries.next_step: Controlled native comparison is pending; native coverage and unresolved budgets prevent qualification.

entries.title: Notify module host revocation without idle probes
entries.invariant: Optional v2 host entrypoint preserves exact v1 ABI; revoke before draining invocation and callbacks before module context destruction.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One bounded callback registry per module instance; subscription unregister waits for in-flight callbacks.
entries.cancellation: Owned resources remain alive through actual work completion and release on owner teardown.
entries.tradeoffs: Legacy modules/hosts retain their 100 ms watchdog; modern idle path issues zero Active requests in the focused test.
entries.next_step: Controlled native comparison is pending; native coverage and unresolved budgets prevent qualification.

entries.title: Push cloud session token changes
entries.invariant: Rotation and fencing notify subscribers immediately; cancellation and session updates precede inbound stream events.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One level-triggered generation watch; carries no credentials.
entries.cancellation: Owned resources remain alive through actual work completion and release on owner teardown.
entries.tradeoffs: Successful host rounds sleep until local/config/module/enable wake; failed provider startup retains five-second retry and does not starve other providers. Provider-owned adaptive network/auth/reconnect deadlines and the legacy V1 lifetime watchdog remain.
entries.next_step: Native resource and platform evidence remain incomplete; do not infer CPU savings from removed timers alone.

entries.title: Wake Windows clipboard capture from native events
entries.invariant: Sequence number remains authoritative; listener failure and pending reads keep reliable polling fallback.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One message-only window, notification thread and native stop event; teardown unregisters and joins.
entries.cancellation: Owned resources remain alive through actual work completion and release on owner teardown.
entries.tradeoffs: macOS polling is retained. Windows source cross-compiles in an isolated harness, but actual Windows behavior and resource use are unmeasured.
entries.next_step: Controlled native comparison is pending; native coverage and unresolved budgets prevent qualification.

entries.title: Gate settled semantic indexing by durable revisions
entries.invariant: Preserve cross-process writes and model integrity.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Separate level-triggered urgent/background generations; settled indexing skips semantic_work and pruning until generation/semantic revision or model scope changes. Disabling/shutdown clears pending queries and caches.
entries.cancellation: Preserve existing cancellation and release ownership after actual work exits.
entries.tradeoffs: The failed filesystem watcher remains rejected. A five-second revision/integrity maintenance wake preserves external Store/process recovery; this is not a zero-wakeup service.
entries.next_step: Resource qualification remains unestablished; native inference/platform measurements and unresolved budgets remain.
entries.previous_attempt: Filesystem watcher failed cross-Store wake validation twice and was removed.

entries.title: Cache History facets by durable revision
entries.invariant: Cache identity includes source/device revision and local device identity; preserve exact existing grouping/labels.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One entry, discarded on identity/revision mismatch, oversized replacement or restore.
entries.cancellation: Preserve existing cancellation and release ownership after actual work exits.
entries.tradeoffs: Avoids repeated facet aggregation; classification SQL predicates remain unchanged. Relevant mutations add revision updates.
entries.next_step: This wave is closed. Resource qualification remains unestablished; no automatic follow-up is scheduled.

entries.title: Push capture state through one runtime watch
entries.invariant: Initial/reconnect/lag snapshots preserve capture/private/health state; both capabilities must be present before retiring fallback polling.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One lazy shared watch per engine, released after the last subscriber; Android screenshot listeners follow settings presentation.

bounds.android_setup_fallback_condition: active stream, focused window, unresolved privileged grants

entries.cancellation: Preserve existing cancellation and release ownership after actual work exits.
entries.tradeoffs: Legacy/unsupported/disconnected runtime backends retain polling. Android setup uses process-local signals, public own-UID AppOps observers and window resume/focus callbacks; a focused unresolved-grant setup stream retains a one-second fallback for READ_LOGS changes lacking a public listener. Signals coalesce to one pending UI task.
entries.next_step: Physical Android and installed Windows runtime/resource evidence remain unavailable; qualification is not established.

entries.title: Authenticate lightweight History previews
entries.invariant: Read metadata and streaming source fingerprint in one SQLite snapshot; domain-separated AEAD binds row ID, nonce, content type and exact metadata. Cache failure falls back to authenticating the original.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Lazy page-scoped resolution and best-effort cache writes; restore/tombstones release entries. Fresh origins, pin/source labels and file availability are applied at presentation.
entries.cancellation: Preserve existing cancellation and release ownership after actual work exits.
entries.tradeoffs: Logical cache limits exclude SQLite metadata, WAL/freelist and page caches. Adds SHA work and best-effort writes; workload-specific CPU/IO tradeoffs require measurement. Full get/copy/save authentication remains unchanged.
entries.next_step: This wave is closed. Resource qualification remains unestablished; no automatic follow-up is scheduled.

entries.title: Report file writer progress without filesystem polling
entries.invariant: Progress carries opaque token and bytes; unary save result alone declares success, preserving rollback/cancellation. Legacy Watch receives no new event kind.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One token subscription during each save; native producer coalesces percentages and shared watch is lazy.
entries.cancellation: Preserve existing cancellation and release ownership after actual work exits.
entries.tradeoffs: Production background file jobs publish typed operation updates through the existing shared runtime connection. Legacy token writer events remain compatible, and non-runtime repository adapters retain their polling fallback. RUN-056 defines durable ownership and cross-engine presentation; native resource qualification remains unestablished.
entries.next_step: This wave is closed. Resource qualification remains unestablished; no automatic follow-up is scheduled.

entries.title: Bound P2P session summaries and preserve catch-up progress
entries.invariant: Separate immutable advertised authorization from page-bounded local comparison metadata; preserve every remote occurrence, exact conflict rules, deferred watermarks and complete persisted-cursor catch-up.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One session-owned workspace; spill uses a random ephemeral SQLCipher key and owned directory/lease. Blocking work retains ownership until actual completion, including caller cancellation.

bounds.local_lookup: One bounded metadata-only query per remote summary page

entries.cancellation: No primary Store connection is retained across network awaits; session completion/error/cancellation drops the workspace after running blocking I/O completes. Startup cleanup respects active cross-process leases. Android uses rustix flock; macOS/Windows retain standard locks.
entries.tradeoffs: Spill adds encrypted disk I/O and metadata lookups; estimated bounds are not a native whole-heap limit. One-pair 10k/four-peer observation showed nearly unchanged sampled peak and slightly longer wall time; no causal speed or RAM improvement is claimed.
entries.next_step: Native process-family, sustained and supported-platform qualification remains incomplete.

entries.title: Evaluate OCR thread-pool spinning
entries.invariant: Preserve all ten OCR routes, results and critical latency; select scheduling policies from equivalent native evidence.
entries.allocation_lifetime: Existing per-invocation OCR worker lifecycle retained.
entries.cancellation: Existing worker cancellation/teardown unchanged.
entries.tradeoffs: Experimental spin-off candidate lowered observed CPU but mixed latency regressed amid browser/backup contention; final text matched all 12 runs. No production change accepted; direct new per-route confidence tracing was unavailable.
entries.next_step: Retain production defaults; no further experiment is scheduled automatically.

entries.title: Runtime-owned file operations and deferred selected sources
entries.owner_module: Core file operations and Flutter transfer presentation
entries.invariant: Selected file registration reads metadata only. File bodies move on explicit actions in bounded chunks. Runtime workers survive presentation closure. Repeated activations reuse the existing native-recorded downloaded path; history clearing removes records only. Presentation or RPC failure never deletes a runtime-owned destination; native completion and cancellation remain authoritative. Individual terminal-history deletion preserves saved paths, downloaded-file mappings and active workers. Visible throughput uses a bounded event-driven monotonic EMA without polling timers.
entries.allocation_lifetime: One original descriptor, digest and 64 KiB block per active file session. Lazy shared runtime watcher exists only while UI consumers listen. Durable operation metadata stays in SQLCipher until the user clears it; UI reads pages rather than retaining all history. Small attempt directories remain available for retry alongside durable history; the runtime removes incomplete files on orderly failure.
entries.cancellation: Explicit Cancel and runtime shutdown stop active workers; closing a UI does not. Interrupted operations retain their terminal reason. Android discards unused persisted source grants on the next selection, preserving live and pending references.
entries.tradeoffs: Deferred selected files depend on original availability rather than an independent encrypted snapshot. Existing snapshot capture remains supported. Persistent operation history and completed Quick Paste downloads consume user-cleared disk space. No measured resource saving or native qualification is claimed. Updates the production contracts of RUN-035, RUN-041 and RUN-053 while preserving non-runtime compatibility paths.
entries.functional_validation: Portable core, runtime, P2P, IPC and Flutter tests; daemon detached-transfer test; Android ARM64 bridge cross-check and Kotlin compilation. Native device and resource evidence are not established.
entries.next_step: Measure application, daemon and worker peaks, steady state and growth on macOS, physical Android and installed Windows; resolve runtime budgets before resource qualification.

entries.title: Stable short-lived macOS Keychain accessor
entries.invariant: Preserve one Keychain item and one accessor identity across app upgrades; authenticate both caller and accessor; reap the one-request process within the existing startup deadline. No resident helper or periodic work.
entries.next_step: Collect same-artifact app, daemon and accessor physical footprint, CPU, startup peaks and repeated-start growth. Isolated functional fixtures do not qualify resource behavior; CPU, wakeup and recovery budgets remain unresolved.

entries.title: Bounded Nearby requests and notification inbox
entries.invariant: One active ceremony, five-second unsolicited request cooldown, existing ten-second handshake and sixty-second confirmation deadlines, 8 KiB untrusted pairing messages and at most 50 display-only session inbox entries. No idle notification polling; existing runtime invalidations and active-session observation drive updates. One shared notification plugin owner preserves response callbacks.
entries.next_step: Measure app, daemon and workers separately and together on all supported platforms, including peak, steady state and repeated request/close growth. Native evidence and applicable resource budgets remain unresolved.
entries.tradeoffs: Adds an explicit untrusted handshake before bilateral numeric comparison. Active pairing retains its existing observer until completion. Inbox history is bounded and session-only. No measured saving or resource qualification is claimed.

entries.title: Animate download-button progress only on byte updates
entries.invariant: Draw progress on the themed button perimeter. Interpolate only when progress changes; unknown totals use a static border; inactive transfers retain no progress widget. Respect reduced motion and retain no repeating ticker or polling timer.
entries.next_step: Measure application and runtime CPU, wakeups and native footprint for active, stalled, idle and repeated transfer states on macOS, Android and Windows. CPU and wakeup budgets remain unresolved in runtime-resource-budgets.json.

entries.title: Bounded authenticated binary file stream
entries.invariant: One versioned authenticated request validates the authoritative file size before streaming. CPF1 binary envelopes preserve exact chunk index and byte length, SHA-256 verification, cancellation, pairing revocation, source privacy checks, partial-output cleanup and single-session admission.
entries.functional_validation: 319 isolated P2P tests, two real encrypted loopback stream tests and three core file-download tests passed; the integrated application candidate requires its final combined validation.
entries.next_step: Qualify the final signed application artifacts on supported platforms. Native app/daemon/worker peak, steady, recovery and growth measurements remain missing; unresolved CPU/wakeup/I/O budgets stay unresolved.

entries.title: Use accelerated Snow crypto with the existing Noise suite
entries.invariant: Snow ring-accelerated uses the maintained RingResolver with the existing default-resolver fallback. Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s, pairing authentication, protocol framing, key identity and integrity requirements remain unchanged.
entries.functional_validation: 319 P2P unit and two full-stream integration tests passed for the isolated crypto variant.

entries.next_step: Measure final installed app, daemon and workers on macOS, physical Android and Windows. Probe RSS and one-off CPU samples do not establish released native memory or resource qualification; runtime budgets remain unchanged.

entries.title: Bound personal-group reconciliation inside existing sync lifetimes
entries.owner_module: copypaste-p2p group and copypaste-cloud group transport
entries.invariant: At most 17 active members including self, 4096 removal identities, 768 KiB per signed snapshot, eight ciphertext rows or 64 catalog entries per page, and 4096 cloud writers/digests per account. Reuse existing workers, adaptive cadence, watch notifications and one Realtime socket. Unchanged local exports avoid cloning state; unchanged imports avoid key derivation and disk writes; unchanged catalogs avoid ciphertext downloads; unchanged cloud snapshots avoid upserts. Derived pairing ids are not retained in the tentative SAS generation index. Membership-only credentials use a separate transport scope and a lazy zeroizing cache of at most 16 entries, invalidated on membership changes; content keys remain bound to certified admission generations. The database maintains a ciphertext digest over nonce plus ciphertext; unchanged catalog digests suppress payload reads while missing or altered own rows force repair. Digest caches hold at most 4096 64-byte hex tokens and are released with the account. An exclusion wake revokes native providers even while a provider command is queued behind network work.
entries.functional_validation: 684 Rust tests passed, including 336 P2P unit tests, two full-stream tests, three signed native Supabase integration tests and a signed-provider exclusion regression cancelling an active HTTP request. Five focused regressions cover the four independent-review findings, including same-nonce ciphertext tampering and pre-persistence admission bounds. Four local PostgreSQL assertion suites, Clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt and whitespace checks passed. One pre-existing semantic-model test remains ignored pending staged ONNX assets. Earlier Flutter Devices validation passed 165 tests before these Rust/SQL fixes; no UI code changed in this fix pass. Installed-platform UI and native resource qualification remain not established.
entries.next_step: Measure candidate application, daemon and module workers separately and together on macOS, physical Android and installed Windows, including peak, steady state, repeated reconciliation and growth. Existing CPU/wakeup/I/O/network/growth budgets remain unresolved; no resource qualification is claimed.
